scope: SIGTERM/SIGINT and repeated stop, outstanding coordinator operations, shutdown deadline, SQLite close races

findings.title: In-flight read-only tool calls raise RangeError: Cannot use a closed database after the drain closes SQLite
findings.evidence: release() closes the store after awaiting only Coordinator-tracked work (src/serve.ts:147). WorkerFiles read-only handlers (src/files.ts:121 store.get after an await on provider.getWorker, src/files.ts:142 store.events) and the lazy redactor secret set (src/security.ts:48 c.store.all(), evaluated on every Redactor.text call, reached from the MCP response path src/mcp.ts:40 and the tool error path src/mcp.ts:60) are neither tracked nor woken, so they resume against a closed database. Observed throw: RangeError: Cannot use a closed database, stack security.ts:48 <- text security.ts:7 <- mcp.ts:40 and security.ts:48 <- text security.ts:7 <- mcp.ts:60. The second site is inside register()'s catch block, so the tool's own error path also throws and no isError result is produced. Contained: no unhandled rejection, no crash, no post-close writes.
findings.reproduction: Reviewer probe outside the checkout: /tmp/rv-probe/probe2.ts patches Store.prototype to record any method invoked after Store.close(), seeds a running worker with the repo's FakeProvider/FakeAgent, starts the server, parks provider.getWorker behind a deferred, fires get_worker_logs, calls handle.stop(), then releases the deferred. Bun 1.4.2, exit 0: DRAIN drained 20ms; POST-CLOSE THROWING CALLS 2 (both store.all from security.ts:48); POST-CLOSE WRITES 0; UNHANDLED []. /tmp/rv-probe/probe-postclose.ts independently saw 3 post-close calls (get, events, all) and 0 unhandled rejections. Why guards miss it: docs/SERVE.md and tests/serve.test.ts:643 cover only wait_for_state_change, which stopWaiters does wake; no guard covers the other read-only handlers or the redactor.
findings.recommendation: Make Store.close() set a closed flag and have read methods return a neutral result (null / []) instead of throwing, so a late reader degrades rather than fails; and/or track WorkerFiles handlers with the same Coordinator.track() accounting used for writes and snapshot the redactor secret set once so redaction never needs a post-shutdown database read.
findings.confidence: reproduced: high for the throw (two independent probes, real SQLite and real HTTP/MCP transport); medium for user-visible impact because api.stop(true) usually force-closes the socket first and masks it

findings.title: A repeated SIGINT/SIGTERM cannot shorten a stuck drain; the operator waits the full 60s default deadline
findings.evidence: onSignal() returns immediately on any signal after the first (src/serve-command.ts:112), and the deadline timer is created only inside the first-signal path (src/serve-command.ts:120). defaultShutdownTimeoutMs is 60000 (src/serve-command.ts:9). A drain blocked on a non-settling provider promise, or on pushBranch bounded by SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120000, src/config.ts:53) which already exceeds the 60s shutdown deadline, therefore always runs to the deadline: the operator's repeated Ctrl-C is dropped and the process exits 70 (forcedShutdownExitCode). Under systemd with TimeoutStopSec below 60s the unit is SIGKILLed, yielding 137 instead of 70 and losing the 'Shutdown deadline exceeded' diagnostic.
findings.reproduction: Deterministic code trace: src/serve-command.ts:112 returns before any deadline handling, and no other code path observes signals; handle.stop() is already owned by the first signal. Corroborated by the existing test tests/serve.test.ts:835, which asserts stdout.split('Shutdown requested') has length 2, i.e. the repeat is deliberately ignored, and by tests/serve.test.ts:892, where the only escape is a 400ms SWARMFORGE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS. Not separately reproduced in a spawned child.
findings.recommendation: Treat a second signal while a drain is in progress as an escalation: shorten to a small grace deadline or exit 70 directly, which is the conventional supervisor-friendly behaviour. Leave the first-signal drain intact so durable state is still preserved on the normal path.
findings.confidence: code-evidenced: high (deterministic from onSignal and corroborated by an existing test); the behaviour is deliberate and documented, hence LOW rather than higher

tests.command: bun install --frozen-lockfile (Bun 1.4.2 at /tmp/bun142/bun-linux-x64) then: bun test tests/serve.test.ts; bun run /tmp/rv-probe/probe-postclose.ts; bun run /tmp/rv-probe/probe2.ts
tests.summary: bun install exit 0 (125 packages, lockfile untouched). bun test tests/serve.test.ts exit 0: 20 pass / 0 fail, 111 expect() calls, 4.42s. Both reviewer probes exit 0; probe2 reported POST-CLOSE THROWING CALLS 2, POST-CLOSE WRITES 0, UNHANDLED []. The system bun is 1.3.14 and cannot read this lockfileVersion 2, so official Bun 1.4.2 was installed under /tmp and the lockfile was never rewritten. No whole-suite run and no compile (out of scope for this reviewer).

limitations: Probes patched Store.prototype from /tmp/rv-probe/, outside the source checkout; no source file was modified and nothing was committed.

All provider and agent calls used the repo's own FakeProvider/FakeAgent from tests/helpers.ts against a throwaway SQLite file in mkdtemp on loopback ports from Bun.serve({port:0}); no real cloud, model provider or infrastructure was contacted.
Post-close behaviour for get_worker_artifact and swarmforge:// resource reads was inferred from the identical WorkerFiles -> store code path as get_worker_logs rather than probed separately.
The second finding was not reproduced in a spawned child process; it is a deterministic read of onSignal corroborated by tests/serve.test.ts:835.
Only tests/serve.test.ts was executed; other test files were read only in part and were not run, being out of this reviewer's scope.
Checkout for review was a disposable git archive of the target SHA at /tmp/rv-serve-drain; /workspace/repo was left on its assigned baseline, unchanged and clean.
No credentials, .env files or secret stores were inspected; all example values are repo-local placeholders.
